newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling stable, trading within narrow band.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling stable, trading within narrow band.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling was stable on Wednesday, quietly trading within a narrow band of 55.30/40 to the dollar, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling average rate of 55.33 from 55.35 against the dollar. Versus the pound, it was posted at 91.03 from 92.92.

"There is a little demand for the shilling, and we are not seeing many inflows from exporters coming in today," one dealer said. "In fact, a few players tried to dip the shilling but basically, there's been no movement of the shilling rate."
Some dealers said investors tried to narrow spreads to try to attract trade.
"There was mild intervention, which sent players on a dollar buying binge. But continued inflows injected fresh strength into the shilling, holding it steady," another dealer said.
A daily report by Banque Indosuez, said there was still room for the shilling to strengthen against the dollar.
The money market was liquid. Overnight rates were quoted between five and ten percent from 10 percent on Tuesday.
